ECOLOGO certified products are made with materials that reduce environmental impact at one or more stages of their life cycle, from raw materials to end of life. About this item

  • 19 PROGRAMMABLE BUTTONS — Armed with ergonomically positioned buttons that provide an arsenal of commands at the fingertips for mapping out the essentials or going all out with advanced macros
  • RAZER HYPERSPEED WIRELESS (2.4 GHZ) AND BLUETOOTH — Unleash seamless, low-latency performance that's 25% faster than other wireless tech or switch to Bluetooth for longer hours of gaming
  • POWERED BY RAZER HYPERSCROLL TECHNOLOGY — Perform repeated commands rapidly or blaze through content in free-spin mode, or activate tactile mode for enhanced precision and satisfying feedback
  • LONG BATTERY LIFE — With up to 400 hours on Bluetooth and 250 hours of seamless low-latency gaming on Razer HyperSpeed Wireless (2.4GHz), last longer in the heat of battle with this mouse before having to replace its battery
  • FOCUS PRO 30K OPTICAL SENSOR — Razer’s brand-new sensor provides flawless tracking performance on a wider variety of surfaces including glass —supported by intelligent functions for enhanced aim and control
  • MECHANICAL MOUSE SWITCHES GEN 2 — With gold-plated contact points, the switches are less prone to degrading and have a longer lifespan of up to 60 million clicks
  • #1 SELLING PC GAMING PERIPHERALS BRAND IN THE U.S. — Source — Circana, Retail Tracking Service, U.S., Dollar Sales, Gaming Designed Mice, Keyboards, and PC Headsets, Jan. 2019- Dec. 2023 combined
  • OPTIMIZE MOUSE ACCURACY — Improve accuracy by disabling the "Enhance pointer precision" option in the Windows mouse settings, and further optimize performance using the Razer Synapse App

Amazon Customer
5 out of 5 stars
It’s great, love the customization
Review is for Razer Naga V2 Hyperspeed, not V2 Pro. I don’t understand most of the other reviews. If the software sucks, just assign the keys once and don’t use it until you need to re-assign the keys. To the guy that said one scroll forward, two scrolls back, maybe don’t use hyperscroll if you’re not comfortable?? lol Took me a week to get used to this mouse(I have only used regular mice before this), and about 2 more weeks to build muscle memory for using 12 buttons. The mouse is great, I have no complaints. Buy from Amazon (not a third party seller) instead of Razer website, so you don’t have to deal with Razer’s crappy customer support. I also see mentions of issues with unintentional clicking, don’t buy sensitive mice if your hands are not used to them, or learn to rest your hand on the mouse instead of squeezing it. When you plug the mouse into a computer, it will automatically download the software. After the installation is complete, you might want to disable it at startup from the task manager. You might have to look up how to assign keys if you’re doing it for the first time, but after you’ve done it once it’s easy. You can set up multiple profiles for different games/softwares, but you will have to switch them using the Razer software. I have been using this mouse for about a month and have not experienced any issues. I will update this review if I do.

    Reviewed in Canada on August 15, 2026
    Size: Naga V2 HyperSpeed
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    Literally the best mouse I've ever owned. Been using it for 7 months. The software is excellent. I'm able to run it with 6 profiles (or more if I wanted to)—12+ shortcuts each—that could output a single key, a combination of keys, a macro, a string of letters or numbers like an email or password—or even a sentence. I can move between profiles like pages with the press of any button I configure. Plus, the hypershift button is elite. It gives me access to another set of configurable shortcuts "hidden" behind each of those 6 profiles and accessible by holding down that hypershift button, so I effectively have 24+ shortcuts for each profile. I basically never have to use my keyboard unless I'm typing (and even then, there's always the on-screen keyboard) or gaming.

    At first, it was easy to accidentally press the buttons when lifting the mouse to reposition it for gaming/navigating, but I just had to let my hand develop the muscle memory over a week or so to be able to reposition it without accidental mashing—and I'm glad I did because this mouse has been a game changer. I don't think I'll ever purchase another mouse without the same capabilities. A USB-C rechargeable 4000+ mWh AA battery from Temu lasts a solid month. Buttons are perfectly responsive. Being able to switch between smooth and step-scrolling is awesome, and the mouse fits snugly in the hand. Easily a 5-star mouse. Totally worth the price, and even more worth it if it's on sale. Superiorly more capable than every alternative.

    It’s great, love the customization

    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.

    Review is for Razer Naga V2 Hyperspeed, not V2 Pro.

    I don’t understand most of the other reviews. If the software sucks, just assign the keys once and don’t use it until you need to re-assign the keys. To the guy that said one scroll forward, two scrolls back, maybe don’t use hyperscroll if you’re not comfortable?? lol

    Took me a week to get used to this mouse(I have only used regular mice before this), and about 2 more weeks to build muscle memory for using 12 buttons. The mouse is great, I have no complaints.

    Buy from Amazon (not a third party seller) instead of Razer website, so you don’t have to deal with Razer’s crappy customer support.

    I also see mentions of issues with unintentional clicking, don’t buy sensitive mice if your hands are not used to them, or learn to rest your hand on the mouse instead of squeezing it.

    When you plug the mouse into a computer, it will automatically download the software. After the installation is complete, you might want to disable it at startup from the task manager. You might have to look up how to assign keys if you’re doing it for the first time, but after you’ve done it once it’s easy. You can set up multiple profiles for different games/softwares, but you will have to switch them using the Razer software.

    I have been using this mouse for about a month and have not experienced any issues. I will update this review if I do.

  • Soban
    3 out of 5 stars
    Good quality but be ready for hunt for the right thumb button
    Reviewed in Canada on February 14, 2026
    Size: Naga V2 HyperSpeed
    Verified Purchase
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    Does it work and have every feature that one would want out of mmo mouse.....yes.

    Then why did I return it..........ergonomics are pretty bad for me. So bad that my hand actually hurts after 5 minutes of use.

    If you ever used a logitech mouse like MX revolution/master or g502 then chances of you liking this mouse will be slimmer specially if this is only your side mouse.

    Reasons why I hate it:

    1- thumb buttons are small and practically indistinguishable. One can argue that you need to practice to get used to it but at my age, going to shaolin temple is not an option. Your thumb will keep seeking for the buttons like the USB stick that is lost in drawer all those things that you never find when you need them.

    2- Shape of mouse is awkward for me. The way i have to grip the mouse is that my fingers are stretched out. mouse is smaller than logitech g502 but still is harder to use and was giving my wrist a hard time. I finally figured out why. The front of the mouse is lower than g502. I wished i could add the pictures but unfortunately i have already returned the mouse. Anyways.........the left and right click button are on lower position than the palm itself (check the sideview at the product page). And therefore your fingers are stretched. so if you are a palmer of the mouse or like to rest your arm on the table when using the mouse then you are bound to have problems.

    I used first razer mouse about 14 years ago.......and 14 years later I have the same complaints. The build quality is good. And since ergonomics is a subjective thing, I cannt complain much and size of the buttons can also be forgiven but indistinguishable buttons is a sin.

    The only thing in this mouse that you wont find in others is free wheel and wheel side clicks.
